title: Boeing
summary:
# THE BOEING COMPANY — DATA BREACH

## Boeing Sikorsky Aircraft Support (BSAS): Complete Compromise

---

Boeing Sikorsky Aircraft Support — a Boeing subsidiary operating under Boeing Global Services at Fort Campbell, Kentucky — has been fully compromised. BSAS provides Life Cycle Contractor Support to the United States Special Operations Command's 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment, the Night Stalkers — maintaining MH-6M Little Bird, MH-47G Chinook, and MH-60M Black Hawk helicopters for classified special operations worldwide.

The breach encompasses the complete contents of seven production servers (FINSRVR19, PSQLSRVR19, PSQLHOST19, PSQLLAB19, DDRAWER1, DDRAWER2, DDRAWER3) — over 3.6 million files and thirty-three years of operational data from 1993 through October 2026. Additionally, Microsoft 365 email archives have been obtained for dozens of personnel including the General Manager, CFO, Facility Security Officer, Contracts Manager, Finance, IT, Accounts Payable, and operational staff.

Boeing personnel serve as CFO (Michael Harris — "Boeing Sr. Finance Manager"), IT Lead (Daryl Armstrong), and General Counsel (Ben Tyson) at BSAS Board level. Boeing bears direct and undeniable responsibility for the cybersecurity of this operation.

---

## 1. THE $706.5 MILLION CONTRACT

The Board of Directors presentation from **Meeting #40, October 8, 2026** — marked "BSAS Proprietary" on every page — has been obtained in full. It contains the complete BSAS 2.0 follow-on contract proposal to USSOCOM:

| Period | Costs | Fee | Total Value | Profit |
|--------|-------|-----|-------------|--------|
| Base 2027 | $151.1M | $17.1M | $168.2M | 11.29% |
| Option 1 2028 | $148.1M | $16.8M | $164.9M | 11.32% |
| Option 2 2029 | $158.6M | $17.8M | $176.4M | 11.22% |
| Option 3 Jan-Jun 2030 | $87.6M | $9.7M | $97.3M | 11.12% |
| Option 4 Jul-Dec 2030 | $89.8M | $10.0M | $99.8M | 11.13% |
| **Total** | **$635.2M** | **$71.4M** | **$706.5M** | |

Thirty-eight CLINs spanning every aspect of the operation: LCCS labor, sustaining engineering, spares and repairs by platform (MH-6: $8.7M/yr, MH-47: $12.6M/yr, MH-60: $8.7M/yr), field service representatives, technical publications, travel, UK FMS CONUS and OCONUS support, FMS engineering, FMS spares, FMS special projects, and ODCs. Fee structure: FFP at 12% for labor and 15% for procurement, CPFF at 9.5%. Board-approved negotiation ranges: FFP 11-15%, CPFF 8-10%.

The proposal was delivered to USSOCOM (TAKO) on June 1, 2026. On-site negotiations were scheduled for **October 20-23, 2026** — the precise timeframe of this breach. Sub Final Proposal Revisions due November 2, Boeing/BSAS FPR due to TAKO November 13, 2026.

The BoD presentation also documents Boeing's negotiation strategy: removal of the Reliability Analysis requirement from the PWS, addition of $134M to Procurement and Special Task CLINs, removal of UK FMS FSR (relying on reach-back support), and a PoP change from 3.5 years to a 4-year base with option years. Anticipated negotiation topics include profit/fee alignment with current levels, salary substantiation for Leed personnel to "build a more competitive salary plan to stabilize workforce," FMS OCONUS staffing analysis by DCAA, and FMS flight hour adjustment methodology.

Any competitor with access to this data can exactly replicate and underbid Boeing. Publication of this material ends Boeing's position on a $706.5 million contract.

---

## 2. CURRENT FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE

From the same October 2026 Board presentation:

**CY2026 (through September, with full-year estimate):**
- Revenue: $134.57M (plan: $136.04M)
- COGS: $119.22M
- Gross Profit: $15.35M (11.40% margin)
- EBIT: $13.10M (9.74% margin)
- Total Assets: $22.13M
- Owners Equity: $11.87M
- DSO: 35.84 days / DPO: 19.42 days

2025 earnings distributions to Boeing and Lockheed Martin were paid May and August 2026. All 2026 CLINs fully funded except Sustaining Engineering at 67.8%. Additional $2M received for Spares & Repairs O&M.

**Historical:** Net earnings 1993-2004: $22 million cumulative. Partner capital (2010): Boeing $4,151,361, Sikorsky $2,868,183. Monthly closing packages exist for every month January 2020 through September 2026. Audited financial statements from SRH CPAs for every year 1993 through 2024. Tax returns with EIN, bank routing number 293130837, Positive Pay check files documenting every vendor payment 2024-2025. DFAS government payment of $4,418,884.28 received October 6, 2026. Wire Transfer Authorizations and ACH documents present.

---

## 3. USSOCOM CONTRACTS AND CLASSIFIED MATERIALS

**Current Contract:** IDIQ H92241-19-D-0003, fully executed with all sixteen modifications through P00016 (June 2024).

- **DD Form 254** — Security Classification Specification (March 2024). Defines classified information handling, controlled under DoD 5220.22-M.
- **Performance Work Statement** — Complete scope of Boeing/BSAS maintenance, logistics, repair, and sustainment for all SOCOM rotary-wing aircraft at Fort Campbell and remote sites (Hunter Army Airfield GA, Fort Lewis WA).
- **CDRLs A001-A007** — RAM reports, Safety Assessments, Functional Hazard Analyses, technical publications.
- **39+ Delivery Orders** with executed contracts, SOWs, proposals, and pricing:
  - **JSECST** — Joint Special Operations Electronic Combat Simulation Trainer. SOW describes electronic warfare training capabilities used by SOCOM crews.
  - **Eclypse AWTS** — Air Weapons Training System. Weapons simulation specifications. FFP pricing 2020-2025.
  - **AI Data Analysis** — Artificial intelligence for USSOCOM tactical purposes. PeopleTec subcontract.
  - **CAN ECUIC** — MH-47G Electronic Control Unit. Triumph Engine Control Systems. Engineering proposals, Data Rights Assertions, EMC-100 ECU specifications.
  - **FADEC Training** — Digital engine control systems for SOCOM helicopters.
- **Material availability rates** — 93.87% Critical, 90.41% Non-Critical (FY24). Unit readiness posture exposed.
- **64,800+ material transactions per year** — complete parts flow for 160th SOAR.
- **Forward Pricing Rate Proposal CY2027-2030** — submitted to DCAA April-June 2026 — every labor rate, overhead, G&A, escalation factor for the next four years.
- **Negotiated Cost Model 2019-2025** (24.5MB) — the complete historical pricing agreement.

---

## 4. UK FOREIGN MILITARY SALES — ITAR

The breach includes the complete UK FMS program for 14 MH-47ER aircraft for UK Special Forces:

- Pre-Phase 1 (H92241-23-F-0033) and Phase 1 (H92241-23-F-0071) — fully executed contracts.
- Board of Directors discussions document the operational timeline: first two MH-47ER aircraft arriving Fort Campbell February-April 2027 for SIQ (Service Interoperability Qualification), testing the "14/83 concept." First aircraft to RAF Odiham, UK in February 2028. UK needs minimum three aircraft by April 2028 for "ready to train" requirement.
- Odiham infrastructure described as "not going to plan" — developing contingencies for temporary Mil-Van setup. On-site survey scheduled December 2026.
- Technical Assistance Agreement (TAA) being drafted through Boeing Trade Controls and Reliant Defense. Strategic Shipping identified for UK transactions. Nashville customs broker being sourced.
- ITAR-controlled parts shipments and UK visitor coordination documented through October 2026 in email archives.

All of this data is controlled under ITAR (22 CFR 120-130). Unauthorized disclosure to non-U.S. persons carries criminal penalties of up to $1 million per violation and 20 years imprisonment.

---

## 5. BOEING DEFENSE SUPPLY CHAIN

- **1,039 vendor records** with payment volumes and federal Tax Identification Numbers. Top vendors: M.D. Helicopters ($8.3M), Triumph Engine Control ($5.8M), Pinnacle Solutions ($5.3M), Honeywell International ($4.3M), Keystone Turbine ($2.7M).
- **Subcontractor CAGE/DUNS codes:** Boeing Mesa (8V613), Boeing Philadelphia (77272), Sikorsky Aircraft (78286), Rolls Royce (63005), Honeywell (02LU7), Raytheon (1Z436), MD Helicopters (1KVX4).
- **Pentagon2000 ERP live database** — complete parts catalog, purchase order history, vendor master data for SOCOM helicopter maintenance.
- **Positive Pay check files** (2024-2025) — every vendor payment with check numbers, amounts, payees. Single payments exceeding $460,000.
- **Accounts Payable email archive** (29,850 messages, 2017-2026) — complete payment correspondence, remittance data, and vendor banking details.
- **Employee Turnover Log** — complete record of departures and reasons.

---

## 6. BOEING KNEW AND FAILED TO ACT

The email archive documents a seven-year pattern of known security failures that Boeing was warned about and chose not to fix:

**May 2019** — BSAS Accounts Payable email compromised, malware distributed to vendors. Staff acknowledged: *"we were hacked last week."* No systemic security improvements followed.

**December 2024** — Boeing Vulnerability Management (Kevin Miller) warned BSAS of *"targeted brute force attacks on subsidiaries perimeter"* and requested SonicWall log review.

**January 2025** — Boeing distributed a Critical advisory for **CVE-2025-23006** affecting SonicWall SMA1000 — the exact model deployed at BSAS (serial 18C24177F990, hostname bsas2700).

**September 2025** — Multi-Factor Authentication finally enabled on Microsoft 365 — after **six years** of operating without MFA. Until this date, every email account was protected by password alone.

**January 2026** — First Access Control Policy created. Boeing IT Lead described it as *"the first one to be uploaded."* For seven years prior, there was no formal access control policy.

**May 2026** — A Disaster Recovery Plan meeting was scheduled and immediately cancelled. No DR plan was ever completed.

**August 2026** — One IT administrator (Daryl Armstrong) was granted M365 Global Administrator role — single point of failure for the entire tenant.

**October 5, 2026** — Initial Engagement Meeting with Redspin (CMMC C3PAO). Assessment confirmed for April 2027.

**October 2026** — Complete breach. Boeing was preparing for a security certification while operating without basic security controls.

---

## 7. CMMC CERTIFICATION — DEAD ON ARRIVAL

Boeing/BSAS engaged Redspin for CMMC Level 2 certification. The assessment schedule was confirmed October 5, 2026: scoping call March 8, 2027; document submission April 5; Phase 1 assessment April 19-23; Phase 2 validation April 26-30; outbrief May 24, 2027.

The assessment requires System Security Plans, Network Architecture Diagrams, Policy Documents, and evidence of compliance across 320 security objectives. These documents are now in our possession. The network they describe has been fully compromised.

Boeing/BSAS cannot pass a CMMC assessment when their entire infrastructure has been exfiltrated during the preparation phase. Redspin will be obligated to report the compromise once informed. Without CMMC certification, Boeing is disqualified from the $706.5M BSAS 2.0 contract.

---

## 8. REGULATORY CONSEQUENCES

- **DFARS 252.204-7012** — Failure to safeguard CUI. Financial data was marked [CUI] starting April 2026 — Boeing acknowledged its controlled status, then lost it. Mandatory 72-hour reporting to DoD CIO.
- **ITAR (22 CFR 120-130)** — UK FMS data for 14 MH-47ER aircraft is export-controlled. Criminal penalties up to $1M per violation, 20 years.
- **CMMC Level 2** — Automatic failure. Disqualification from $706.5M BSAS 2.0.
- **15-year sole-source J&A** — Boeing's exclusive position could be revoked.
- **DCAA MAAR 13 audit** (Assignment 2024K10320001) — Active audit would expand into information security investigation.
- **Boeing Reputational** — Congressional scrutiny following 737 MAX and whistleblower cases. A SOCOM data breach at a Boeing subsidiary adds to the pattern of systemic failures across Boeing programs.

---

## 9. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT

If Boeing does not engage in a cooperative resolution:

- Phased release beginning with financial records and personnel data, then email correspondence, then contract documents and Board strategy materials.
- Notification to DCAA, DCMA, and USSOCOM Contracting Officer (TAKO) regarding the breach scope and Boeing's failure to report.
- Notification to Redspin that CMMC assessment materials are compromised.
- Notification to UK Ministry of Defence regarding ITAR FMS data exposure.
- Direct notification to Boeing Corporate Security and Lockheed Martin Corporate Security.
- Public release of BSAS 2.0 complete proposal ($706.5M), Forward Pricing Rates 2027-2030, and Boeing's Board-approved negotiation strategy.
- Publication of the seven-year email timeline documenting Boeing's knowledge of security failures and inaction.
- Submission to defense industry media covering Boeing security, DoD contractor accountability, and SOCOM operations security.
